amendment.reason: BoldHorizon (hachi-issue-16): the original variant expressed coverage as the share of 5-minute slots holding a sample (12/12 = 1.0 at full 5-minute cadence), while served Apple features report distinct sampled minutes / 60 (12/60 = 0.2), so its coverage gate was not transferable. Declared after the original variant had been scored; it changes the coverage denominator only. Under thinning, minute coverage >= 0.10 holds exactly when the slot rule did, so the admitted hours are identical and no gate is chosen from scores. Evidence about cadence only: not a real Apple device, wear or physiology validation.

density_gate.justification: Coverage is computed exactly as the Apple serving helper does (hachi.data.apple_health.hourly, rule apple-hour-end-sealed-native-v1): distinct sampled start minutes / 60, with a bin null only when empty. At 5-minute cadence an hour holds at most 12 samples, so coverage is at most 0.2 and every typical Apple hour reports 0.2. The frozen protocol admits an hour with >= 30 covered minutes; under 5-minute thinning those span >= 6 slots, i.e. >= 6 distinct sampled minutes: coverage >= 0.10 with >= 6 samples is the frozen rule at this cadence in the Apple helper's own denominator. The audit confirms it: all 46,406 frozen-admitted hours keep coverage >= 0.10 (min 0.10, p01 0.133, median 0.20); coverage >= 0.15 would drop 1.1% of them with no structural basis.

evaluation.overlap_note: Native CPU comparators; new-person validation with explicitly permitted personal history. PMData clock mapping and historical availability are documented assumptions, not observed synchronization.
